groups.rationale: Records 2 and 55 both describe under-updating beliefs when new evidence arrives. Record 171 instead describes remembered magnitudes or probabilities regressing toward less extreme values, so matching the title is not enough to merge it with the belief-updating construct.

evidence.title: The neural basis of belief updating and rational decision making
evidence.note: Defines conservatism in belief updating as overweighting prior information relative to new information.

groups.reviewNote: The memory/regressive label for record 171 still needs a primary-source terminology review before any rename.

groups.rationale: Both records describe outcome knowledge making past events seem more predictable than they were in foresight.

evidence.title: Hindsight is not equal to foresight: The effect of outcome knowledge on judgment under uncertainty
evidence.note: Foundational experimental paper on outcome knowledge increasing perceived prior predictability.

evidence.title: Fifty years of hindsight bias research—Reflection on Fischhoff (1975)
evidence.note: Recent reflection by Fischhoff describes the same core construct.

groups.rationale: Both records describe repetition or familiarity increasing perceived truth without adding probative evidence.

evidence.title: Frequency and the conference of referential validity
evidence.note: Seminal demonstration that repeated statements receive higher validity judgments.

evidence.title: The effects of repetition frequency on the illusory truth effect
evidence.note: Replicates the repetition-based increase in perceived truth and examines dose-response shape.

groups.rationale: Both records describe subjective probability judgments in which unpacked components receive more total judged probability than the packed event.

evidence.title: Support theory: A nonextensional representation of subjective probability
evidence.note: Introduces support theory and reports subadditivity in subjective probability judgments.

evidence.title: Unpacking, repacking, and anchoring: advances in support theory
evidence.note: Demonstrates implicit and explicit subadditivity in probability and frequency judgments.
